data.name: Anugraha
data.gender_notes: Anugraha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Anugraha is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘anu’ meaning ‘towards’ and ‘graha’ meaning ‘grasping’. It signifies the act of extending grace, blessings towards someone. In Hindu mythology, Anugraha is also the name of a goddess, considered the embodiment of compassionate grace. The name Anugraha carries the meaning “Grace, Blessing” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Anugraha usually hope their child will grow to embody grace, blessing and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of compassionate grace and divine blessings.
data.etymology: Anugraha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Grace, Blessing.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Anugraha total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_sanskrit.name: अनुग्रह
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: अनुग्रहः (Anugrahah) is a Sanskrit word that refers to divine grace, compassion, and mercy. It is derived from the root word 'anu' (towards) and 'grah' (grasps), meaning 'to grasp towards'. In Hinduism, Anugrah is often depicted as a divine power that showers blessings upon devotees. It is also the name of several Hindu gods and goddesses, including Ganesha, Durga, and Vishnu, who are believed to bestow grace and mercy upon their devotees.

in_hindi.name: अनुग्रह
in_hindi.long_meaning: अनुग्रह (Anugrah) हिंदी में 'प्रसाद' (prasad - grace), 'प्रसन्नता' (prasanna-tā - happiness), और 'आशा' (āśā - hope) के साथ-साथ संबद्ध है।

in_tamil.name: அனுக்ரவா

in_telugu.name: అనుగ్రాధ
